population.span: We conducted a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 18,924 patients who had an acute coronary syndrome 1 to 12 months earlier

endpoint.span: The primary end point was a composite of death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, fatal or nonfatal ischemic stroke, or unstable angina requiring hospitalization.

estimate.span: A composite primary end-point event occurred in 903 patients (9.5%) in the alirocumab group and in 1052 patients (11.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 0.93; P<0.001).

ci.span: A composite primary end-point event occurred in 903 patients (9.5%) in the alirocumab group and in 1052 patients (11.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 0.93; P<0.001).

analysis_set.span: Intent-to-treat (ITT) population included all randomized participants.

treatment_strategy.span: Patients were randomly assigned to receive alirocumab subcutaneously at a dose of 75 mg (9462 patients) or matching placebo (9462 patients) every 2 weeks. The dose of alirocumab was adjusted under blinded conditions to target an LDL cholesterol level of 25 to 50 mg per deciliter (0.6 to 1.3 mmol per liter).

follow_up.span: The median duration of follow-up was 2.8 years.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Recent ACS patients fall within the ASCVD population; registry eligibility requires age 40 or older, and the primary outcome uses ITT.

notes: Registry evidence is used for the primary outcome analysis set. The registry reports its observation window as randomization up to 64 months; the abstract reports median follow-up of 2.8 years. Background statin therapy was high-intensity or maximum tolerated. No full text is held.
